name: NJM4556 / NJM4556A (dual high-output-current bipolar, 70 mA)
tagline: JRC's 70 mA dual that drives 150 ohm loads directly. It is the paralleled output stage of NwAvGuy's O2 and a staple of Japanese DIY headphone amps.
technology: Bipolar dual op-amp with a high-current output stage (+/-70 mA into 150 ohm at +/-10.5 V). The input differential pair is PNP in the datasheet equivalent circuit, in NJR's own PSpice macromodels (Version 1 and 2) and in the 2007 Bee Technologies model. Supply is +/-2 V to +/-18 V. The datasheet says it combines many NJM4558 features with 150 ohm drive capability. The Japanese search summary describes it as a 4558 with a reinforced output stage. On the typical curve at +/-15 V, the output sources about 100 mA and sinks about 200 mA before swing collapses.
manufacturers: JRC / New Japan Radio Co., Ltd. (New JRC, NJR)
Nisshinbo Micro Devices Inc. (successor to New JRC)
NEC (uPC4556 uses the same number but is a different, decompensated dual op-amp. It is NOT an NJM4556 second source; listed only so the two are not confused)

part_numbers.notes: DIP8. This is the package used in O2 builds; FreeDSP-G also uses it, labelled 'For Headphones Amp Low Impedance Drive Capability'. The EN 20250306 datasheet prints 'NJM4556AD and NJM4556AL are the NRND products' (confirmed from the search-result title of the vendor PDF). A Japanese blog (foxtango101, April 2023) reported NJM4556A among the ex-JRC op-amps designated maintenance products (保守品). Pd 700 mW.
SIP8. NRND in the 20250306 datasheet. Sold by Akizuki Denshi (catalog g111235) and by LCSC (C78948, which hosts a datasheet copy). Pd 800 mW.

DMP8. This is JRC's wider-body SOP and does not fit a JEDEC 3.9 mm SOIC-8 footprint; body about 5.0 mm, lead span about 6.8 mm, per community footprints only. Pd 300 mW. NJM4556AM-TE1 is listed at RS (2413462 / 2413463, '8MHz, 8-Pin DMP'). It is used in the smartstand USB DAC/amp rev A (2016) and in the Roland AC-90 phones amp (IC18). Swing and ICMR are specified at V+=9 V/V-=0 V with 40 mA source/sink.

SSOP8. Pd 250 mW. NJM4556AV-TE1 is listed at RS (SE 2444516: '8MHz, 4 -> 36 V, 8-Pin SSOP8'; JP 2444515: '18V, 8 MHz, 3 V/us, SSOP-8') and at diyaudiocart. Used in Eurorack headphone modules (ramphands Exits, fablabnk HeadPho).

reputation.summary: It is valued for current drive rather than for a distinctive sound. NwAvGuy used NJM4556A in the current-gain (output) stage of the Objective2 (O2), with both halves paralleled per channel. An earlier search summary of his 'O2 Details' page paraphrased him as saying no other dual DIP8 op-amp delivered as much current at as low distortion ('killed everything else'); this pass did not re-confirm that wording. The O2 made it a default DIY headphone driver, reused in O2/ODA derivatives, Eurorack headphone modules and other projects. Japanese DIY sources call it a standard (定番) headphone-amp chip, and say it sounds surprisingly good for about 30 yen. One Japanese listening comparison (audio-simulation.net, 2019) found it more energetic but rougher in texture than the NJM4580. It also appears in commercial gear: one 2018 owner's Behringer UCA202 had a 4556A, and the Roland AC-90 uses NJM4556AM in its phones amp.
sonic_descriptors: energetic / lively (vs NJM4580; single Japanese listening test)
surprisingly good for the price (Japanese DIY summary)
clean, low-distortion current drive (NwAvGuy O2 testing)
typical_uses: O2 / ODA headphone amp output stage (paralleled sections)
DIY and kit headphone amps in Japan (e.g. aitendo kits)
USB audio interface headphone outputs (one 2018 teardown of a Behringer UCA202)
caveats: The DIP8 (NJM4556AD) and SIP8 (AL) versions are NRND per the March 2025 Nisshinbo datasheet. A maintenance-product (保守品) designation was reported in April 2023. The SMD AM and AV versions continue.
The SMD packages are JRC DMP8 (wider body than a 3.9 mm JEDEC SOIC-8) and SSOP8, so footprints differ.
Package dissipation limits are low (DMP8 300 mW, SSOP8 250 mW), and quiescent current is 9 mA typ per package. Derate for high rails and low-impedance headphones.
Speed is modest (3 V/us, 8 MHz). The typical THD at 20 kHz rises steeply with output level (about 0.2% at 10 Vrms into 200 ohm).
High offset (6 mV max) and bias current (500 nA max) matter in DC-coupled designs like the O2.
Its reputation rests on drive capability rather than a distinctive sound. The sonic descriptors come from single listening reports.

A '4556' on vintage boards may be NEC's uPC4556. That part is decompensated (stable only at gain >= 20 dB), so it is not a substitute for an NJM4556 in a unity-gain buffer. It may also be a Yamaha house-marked part.

silicon_changes.when: 1980s (uPC4556 on late-1980s Taito boards per MAME notes)
silicon_changes.identification: Check the prefix and logo, not the digits. NEC 'uPC4556' (DIP8, C suffix) is a different device from JRC 'NJM4556'/'NJM4556A'.
silicon_changes.summary: Same '4556' number, different silicon. NEC's uPC4556 is a decompensated high-speed dual derived from its uPC4558 (20 MHz GBW guaranteed at gain > 20 dB, 5 V/us). JRC's NJM4556/NJM4556A is an internally compensated 70 mA / 150 ohm line and headphone driver, used at unity gain in the O2 output stage.

spec_deltas.before: NJM4556A: internally compensated; used as a unity-gain buffer in the O2
spec_deltas.after: uPC4556: decompensated; GBW guaranteed only at gain >= 20 dB
not seen in datasheet summaries (no 150 ohm drive claim)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: A uPC4556 placed in an NJM4556 socket at unity or low gain (e.g. the O2 output buffer) risks oscillation, and its heavy-load drive is unknown. An NJM4556A replacing a uPC4556 in a high-gain vintage stage would lose bandwidth and slew rate.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: high - a decompensated part is not a drop-in for unity-gain buffer or driver roles. The pinout is the standard dual, but the stability requirements differ.
silicon_changes.verification: Not re-searched in this pass (medium confidence, second-source kind, not from the sweep). Kept as assembled from the earlier datasheet-mirror research.

silicon_changes.summary: The part number moved from NJM4556 to NJM4556A. No vendor or web document found says whether this was a new die, a process change or a re-specification. The non-A datasheet (alldatasheet 7450, datasheetbank, octopart NJM4556S) carries the same 'DUAL HIGH CURRENT OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIER' title and 70 mA / 150 ohm role, but no side-by-side spec comparison was retrieved. A forum post calls the A 'the same as the original, but with an A'. The discovery hint that the A is a 'respecified' NJM4556 remains unconfirmed.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low (presumed) - same function, same dual 8-pin op-amp role and same 70 mA / 150 ohm headline, but the non-A detailed limits (output current, minimum supply, noise) are unverified.
silicon_changes.verification: Two WebSearches found no document explaining how the A differs from the non-A. They confirmed that both share the dual-high-current title and 70 mA / 150 ohm headline, found an NJM4556L listing that contradicts the S-to-L rule, and dated the A datasheet to 2003-03-18 (DigiKey mirror). Kept as renumbering, low confidence.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit or remarking reports for NJM4556/NJM4556A were found; search coverage was limited. eBay listings of NJM4556AD advertised as '"Original" JRC' show that DIP stock now circulates on the grey market after the NRND notice; the 2023 保守品 report and the March 2025 datasheet both mark AD/AL as NRND. Remarked 4558/4559-class duals would not deliver 70 mA (unverified risk). Salvaged vintage '4556' parts may be NEC uPC4556, a decompensated part that is unstable at unity gain and not an equivalent, or Yamaha house-marked YM4556 parts. A practical check: at +/-15 V a genuine NJM4556A should hold about +/-11 V into 150 ohm (datasheet min +/-10.5 V), draw about 9 mA per package, and be stable as a unity-gain follower. Buy from authorized Nisshinbo distributors.

The original NJM4556 (non-A) datasheet was not read (alldatasheet 7450, datasheetbank). Unknown: its specs, and whether NJM4556A is a new die or a re-specification.

uPC4556: the decompensated design and 20 MHz / 5 V/us figures are known from mirror summaries. Its output-current rating and minimum stable gain wording should be read from the NEC sheet (alldatasheet 6766).
Yamaha 'YM4556D' house-marked parts are known only from forum text; unconfirmed.
